sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The true alternative does not bind the normal-operational/expected-load context and the local-strength capacity to the same designCondition: the universal hasDesignCondition constraint and the conditional hasDesignCondition constraint are separate existential property constraints, so distinct design-condition nodes can satisfy them and duplicate the relationship. Restructure the alternatives so the true branch requires one hasDesignCondition value satisfying normalOperationalConditions=true, designConditionExpectedLoad, and designConditionLocalStrengthCapacity, while the false branch requires one hasDesignCondition value satisfying the normal-operational/expected-load shape; keep localIcePressure and the capacity >= localIcePressure DIRECT_CHECK only in the true branch, and retain all existing ship-owned operands, serviceLife, extremeLoad, and applicability terms.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the Complex-readiness encoding to cover the full verified applicability and conditional semantics. In addition to thrusterType and mainPropulsionThruster, represent the declared normal-operational/expected-load context and the condition that the thruster body is designed for extreme loads, using the supplied canonical terms normalOperationalConditions and extremeLoad on their authoritative owners. Link these conditions to the relevant design condition rather than requiring localIcePressure and local-strength capacity unconditionally for every ship. Preserve the required ship-to-designCondition path, all declared load operands, the capacity result, kilonewton/megapascal quantity structures, and the DIRECT_CHECK capacity >= localIcePressure comparison. Do not invent a convenience applicability boolean or relocate properties to another owner.

Repair the conditional semantics while preserving the prior instruction. The current sh:or makes the entire load/design-condition bundle mandatory whenever mainPropulsionThruster is true, regardless of whether the thruster body is designed for extreme loads, and the false branch omits all required applicability evidence. Encode the supplied canonical thrusterBodyLocalStrength condition on its authoritative ship owner and make the localIcePressure, designConditionLocalStrengthCapacity, and capacity >= localIcePressure DIRECT_CHECK conditional on that condition. Link the normalOperationalConditions and designConditionExpectedLoad values through the required hasDesignCondition path, and retain all declared load operands propellerIceInteractionLoad and thrusterBodyIceInteractionLoad with their required kN quantity structures. Do not use extremeLoad as a substitute for the designed-for-extreme-load condition; it is a load quantity, not the conditional selector. Preserve thrusterType and mainPropulsionThruster applicability and do not require the conditional local-pressure/capacity branch unconditionally.

Repair the readiness shape before freezing. Remove the nltl:hasDesignCondition property from gen:LocalStrengthConditionShape: this shape is applied to the designCondition node and currently demands an erroneous nested design condition, duplicating the ship-to-designCondition relationship. Keep nltl:designConditionLocalStrengthCapacity and the DIRECT_CHECK comparison on that designCondition, with nltl:localIcePressure on the ship. Preserve the existing false/true thrusterBodyLocalStrength alternatives, normalOperationalConditions and expected-load context, all required ship-owned interaction loads, and the separate extremeLoad quantity; extremeLoad must not serve as the applicability selector. Also encode the supplied serviceLife term on its authoritative ship owner if it is intended to cover the stated service-life scope.
